digest.component_or_area: completion verification and ticket-store access patterns
propositions: Full ticket-store materialization consumes 135–235 seconds for 5,500 directories and 132,000 files; scoped Git-pinned reads reduce this to ~29 ms by lazily materializing only named tickets at a captured commit OID.

Pinned Git tree reads (git rev-parse/ls-tree/cat-file) against a real 86b18cb9… tracker show p50/p90/max latencies of 9–12/12–16/49–62 ms per operation, with byte-identical reads across concurrent live mutations to a later revision 6e7f6b56….

Validation of pinned reads must track exact ticket state, direct children, transitive descendants, relation membership, and global resolver inputs such as .bridge_state/bindings.json; ticket-only or tree-only equality is insufficient to catch hierarchy/link changes.

Current rebar transition_close writes COMPLETION_VERDICT before STATUS and SIGNATURE in separate transactions, risking partial/incomplete closure artifacts; atomic bundling into one local commit under the tracker lock is required before publication.

Parallel completion reviews can collide on shared per-criterion .tmp cache paths and may mix pinned code/tickets with live-checkout prefetch; conflict detection and receipt validation must distinguish state-bearing inputs from operation-owned observability.

Design requires short critical section (tracker HEAD assertion + prepared bundle commit + fast-forward ref update) outside lock; all verification, signing, and event construction must proceed against the pinned OID and validate deltas on retry if HEAD advances.
